html:
SMTO-EXE-0240 — The selected Gateway can't do this Docker task

GUID: f3718b05-b79a-520c-9f38-658f5087de4d
Slug: docker-target-capability-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) that this task uses is missing a Docker part needed for this request. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select the Gateway, select Check connection, and read its Capabilities list for entries starting with docker_. The list shows exactly which Docker features this Gateway can use, such as docker_build for builds or docker_compose for Compose.
  2. If the needed feature is missing, ask the person who manages that computer to install it (Docker Compose or Buildx) or rerun the Gateway installer there, without removing the Gateway. Reinstalling in place repairs missing parts while keeping the Gateway's pairing, settings and saved files.
  3. If that Gateway runs on Windows, open the Execution target menu in the composer and choose a Linux or macOS Gateway instead. SMTO's Docker support only works with Docker on Linux or macOS computers.
  4. After the Gateway shows the feature, start a new task for the Docker request. Tasks that already started keep the list of features the Gateway had when they began.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's Capabilities list shows the needed docker_ entry and a new task completes the Docker request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages that computer. Don't delete or re-pair the Gateway to fix this; its pairing, credentials and saved files are not the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway lacks the Docker capability this operation needs: a supported local Unix-socket Engine endpoint (Windows and remote endpoints are unsupported), the Docker SDK extra for builds, the Compose v2 plugin, a usable Buildx build-cache backend, or Docker transport support in the Gateway itself.

What this means

  • The adapter lacks a supported local Unix-socket transport, required Docker SDK/CLI/Buildx capability or a usable build-cache backend. Platform and dependency failures are distinct prerequisites. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The adapter lacks a supported local Unix-socket transport, required Docker SDK/CLI/Buildx capability or a usable build-cache backend. Platform and dependency failures are distinct prerequisites.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Docker readiness and the exact local endpoint/feature, distinguishing unsupported platform from a missing or failed dependency.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's capability tags (docker_engine, docker_registry, docker_build, docker_compose, docker_build_cache) in Settings › Setup › Gateways. Ensure GATEWAY_DOCKER_ENDPOINT is a local unix:/// socket the Gateway account can access; install python -m pip install -e '.[docker]' for builds, the system Docker Compose v2 plugin for Compose, and Buildx for build cache, or rerun the Gateway installer (./src/gateway_agent/install.sh, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh, .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1) as the Gateway account. Restart the Gateway after active work settles, refresh capabilities, and start a new task.
  • Inspect the selected Gateway Docker readiness. If its Docker SDK, CLI or Buildx plugin is missing or incompatible, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. Engine availability, socket permissions and unsupported operations require their own remedy.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway advertises the supported local transport and required operation capability.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
